identity.name: Bitterroot
identity.description: Bitterroot is a vast, untamed world of ancient forests, drowned valleys, rugged mountains, and isolated settlements. No humans exist here. Its people are intelligent, speaking beastfolk and feral-bodied peoples with many different body forms, cultures, instincts, and ways of life. Civilization remains pre-industrial. Communities survive through hunting, farming, craftsmanship, trade, and knowledge passed between generations. Beyond their borders lie forgotten paths, territorial creatures, old ruins, violent weather, and forces buried beneath the land. Bitterroot is intimate, dangerous, and hopeful. Families can be broken or rebuilt, friendships may become lifelong bonds, and old choices leave scars across generations. Characters are free to grow, travel, form relationships, establish homes, and change the world around them. This is a living reality without a predetermined ending.

rules.technology: Pre-industrial. Hand tools, fire, animal power, simple water power, craft production, farming, hunting, fishing, trade, and local construction are normal. No modern industry, engines, firearms, electrical infrastructure, or digital technology.
rules.magicPhysics: No universal magic system is assumed. Supernatural forces, unusual species traits, and buried phenomena exist only where Bitterroot canon establishes them.
rules.society: Communities are organized through families, households, clans, tribes, bands, villages, and other local societies. Authority is local and practical rather than enforced by a single world government.
constraints: All intelligent peoples are beastfolk, anthropomorphic peoples, or intelligent feral-bodied peoples.
Bitterroot remains pre-industrial unless later canon explicitly changes a place or era.
Different intelligent peoples may have very different body forms while still speaking, building communities, and participating in society.
The world has no predetermined ending. Actions and remembered events may permanently change places, families, societies, and relationships.
Species heritage can influence cultural traditions, but it does not dictate an individual's personality, morality, profession, or musical taste.
Every major Bitterroot place may develop its own dominant and secondary species mix, folk tradition, instruments, rhythms, and contemporary genre identity.

lore.history: Bitterroot has been shaped by old floods, drowned valleys, changing trails, isolated settlements, and generations of local survival. The Howling Hills carry the scars of a catastrophic flooding remembered across the region. Much of the deeper history remains intentionally open for authored canon rather than being filled with assumptions.
lore.cultures: Bitterroot contains many local ways of life rather than one universal culture. Families, clans, tribes, bands, households, and settlements may each preserve their own customs, dialects, loyalties, hunting grounds, seasonal routes, and relationships with neighboring peoples.
lore.customs: Customs vary by place and people. Kinship, adoption, guardianship, hospitality, territory, seasonal movement, craft, trade, and shared memory can all matter. Local custom should be authored where needed instead of treated as a single rule for the whole world.
importantFacts: Whispering Woods, Bitterroot Bluffs, Bitterroot Peak, Howling Hills, and Bitterroot Orphanage are established places.
Shadow Creek, Moonflower Meadow, and Hidden Haven Cave are established places within Whispering Woods.
Intelligent inhabitants may be upright, partially anthropomorphic, or feral-bodied.
The Howling Hills were changed by a major flood whose effects still shape the landscape and memory of the region.

species.name: Bitterroot beastfolk
species.description: The intelligent speaking peoples of Bitterroot. Body form varies widely between peoples and individuals, from strongly anthropomorphic to feral-bodied forms. No human population exists.

species.name: Werewolf
species.description: Intelligent speaking werewolves of Bitterroot. Ragna Holt and Pip Holt are upright feral werewolves.

species.name: Foxfolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic fox peoples of Bitterroot. Fox communities are often associated with quick social reading, expressive performance, negotiation, trade, nightlife, improvisation, and fast-moving local cultures.

socialCharacter: strong traditions of bargaining and performance
culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Fast, nimble, improvisational folk built around dance, storytelling, competitive solos, and playful rhythmic turns.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Syncopated dance rhythms, quick tempo shifts, sudden stops, and call-and-response figures.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Fast storytelling, teasing verses, call-and-response, and improvised lyrical exchanges.

species.name: Bearfolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic bear peoples of Bitterroot. Bear communities commonly favor physically grounded craft, communal labor, heavy celebration, deep vocal traditions, and music that emphasizes weight, resonance, and endurance.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Heavy, slow folk with large drums, low strings, stomping rhythms, and resonant group singing.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Broad pulses, heavy downbeats, slow dances, and physically forceful communal rhythms.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Deep solo voices, drones, and massed low choruses.

species.name: Cervidfolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic deer, elk, and related cervid peoples of Bitterroot. Their cultures often develop ceremonial, melodic, seasonal, and landscape-centered traditions with strong regional variation.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Spacious ceremonial folk using layered melody, bells, flutes, bowed strings, and measured dance.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Measured dances, flowing meters, long phrases, and gradual crescendos.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Layered harmonies, sustained melodic lines, and ceremonial group singing.

species.name: Harefolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic rabbits and hares of Bitterroot. Harefolk communities are frequently known for quick communal dances, rapid instrumental traditions, busy markets, and music built for movement.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Fast dance folk driven by rapid fiddle, plucked strings, clapping, whistles, and compact percussion.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Fast repeating patterns, hopping accents, sudden bursts, and relentless dance momentum.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Quick refrains, communal choruses, and short energetic verses.

species.name: Boarfolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic boar peoples of Bitterroot. Boarfolk traditions often prize blunt expression, physical celebration, endurance, territorial pride, and loud communal performance.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Rough, loud folk centered on war drums, horn calls, shouted refrains, and forceful string rhythms.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Driving straight beats, pounding marches, and aggressive dance rhythms.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Shouted choruses, gravelly solos, drinking songs, and competitive chants.

species.name: Badgerfolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic badger peoples of Bitterroot. Badger communities often grow around dense local networks, practical crafts, digging or stonework traditions, and stubbornly persistent musical forms.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Dense rhythmic folk built from repetitive work patterns, low strings, percussion, and communal chants.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Repetitive grooves, layered work rhythms, and gradually intensifying patterns.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Work chants, low group singing, and terse narrative songs.

species.name: Felinefolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic feline peoples of Bitterroot. Feline communities often develop precise, expressive performance traditions with strong attention to timing, movement, personal style, and musical finesse.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Precise, expressive folk using plucked strings, hand drums, ornamented melody, and controlled rhythmic tension.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Flexible syncopation, graceful pauses, intricate meter, and dance-focused phrasing.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Expressive solo voices, ornamentation, close harmonies, and intimate performance.

species.name: Avianfolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic bird peoples of Bitterroot. Avian traditions often emphasize voice, height, distance, layered calls, aerial symbolism, and music that travels clearly across open spaces.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Voice-led folk with whistles, flutes, layered harmony, bright percussion, and long-distance call patterns.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Interlocking patterns, fast ornamentation, suspended phrases, and soaring melodic arcs.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Complex harmony, antiphonal calls, whistles, and high sustained lines.

species.name: Otterfolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic otter peoples of Bitterroot. Otter communities are frequently river- or coast-oriented and favor social, rhythmic, playful musical traditions built around movement and communal gathering.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Buoyant river folk with hand drums, whistles, fiddles, clapping, and strongly social dance forms.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Bouncy syncopation, rolling dance grooves, and rhythms inspired by rowing and water work.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Group refrains, humorous verses, and fast communal singing.

species.name: Reptilefolk
species.description: Anthropomorphic reptilian peoples of Bitterroot. Reptilefolk cultures vary widely, but many regional traditions favor hypnotic repetition, percussion, drones, ritual pacing, and strong environmental adaptation.

culturalProfile.note: Regional cultures may reshape this baseline. Species heritage influences traditions, but individuals and settlements are not required to conform to one personality or genre.

musicCulture.folkCore: Sparse, hypnotic folk built from drums, drones, rattles, low pipes, and repetitive ceremonial patterns.
musicCulture.rhythmicCharacter: Steady repetition, polyrhythm, slow-building loops, and ritual pulse.
musicCulture.vocalTradition: Chanted lines, low drones, sparse solo phrases, and cyclical refrains.

locations.name: Bitterroot
locations.description: The greater land and living reality known as Bitterroot, containing the Howling Hills and the established regions nested within them.

locations.name: Howling Hills
locations.description: A broad and dangerous major region marked by rugged country, old flood scars, isolated communities, forests, bluffs, and high ground.

locations.name: Whispering Woods
locations.description: An old forest region threaded by Shadow Creek. Moonflower Meadow and Hidden Haven Cave lie within the woods. Paths can be difficult to follow and communities live close to the land.

locations.name: Moonflower Meadow
locations.description: A meadow within Whispering Woods associated with the moonflowers that give it its name.

locations.name: Shadow Creek
locations.description: A creek running through Whispering Woods and forming a natural landmark and route through the forest.

locations.name: Hidden Haven Cave
locations.description: A concealed cave within Whispering Woods. Its exact history and uses remain open for authored canon.

locations.name: Bitterroot Bluffs
locations.description: Rugged bluff country within the Howling Hills, with difficult approaches and exposed terrain.

locations.name: Bitterroot Peak
locations.description: High mountain country rising above the surrounding lands. Weather, elevation, and isolation shape travel here.

locations.name: Bitterroot Orphanage
locations.description: An established orphanage within the Howling Hills. It is a home and institution for young residents without a stable family home, with its deeper history left to Bitterroot canon.

locations.name: Splitpine Reach
locations.description: Cold upland country within the Howling Hills. Brackenjaw Enclave lies here, and Boundary Wardens patrol its trails and marked borders.

locations.name: Brackenjaw Enclave
locations.description: A pre-industrial settlement in Splitpine Reach. Ragna Holt and Pip Holt live here among the Brackenjaw community.

locations.name: Brackenjaw Ranger Station
locations.description: The ranger station used by Brackenjaw Boundary Wardens. Ragna works from here, and Pip has grown up around patrol maps, gear, chores, and ranger routines.

locations.name: Brackenjaw Eastern Boundary
locations.description: The eastern boundary of Brackenjaw territory, watched and patrolled by Boundary Wardens including Ragna Holt.

locations.name: Warning Stones
locations.description: Marked boundary stones used to warn travelers before they cross deeper into Brackenjaw territory.

factions.name: Boundary Wardens
factions.description: Brackenjaw rangers responsible for patrol work, boundary defense, trail security, threat assessment, and keeping Splitpine Reach defensible. Their work values preparedness, practical judgment, clear warnings, and decisive action when a credible threat appears.

societies.name: Howling Hills Peoples
societies.description: A broad World Forge grouping for the independent peoples of the Howling Hills. It does not imply a single centralized state and can be split or renamed as individual cultures are authored.
societies.origin: Local families, clans, tribes, bands, households, and settlements developed across the Howling Hills over generations.
societies.territoryNotes: A loose regional grouping rather than exclusive ownership of every place inside the Howling Hills.
societies.seasonalMovement: Varies by local people and livelihood.
societies.kinshipBasis: Family, descent, adoption, guardianship, clan ties, and local bonds vary between communities.
societies.membershipRules: Determined locally by the family, clan, tribe, band, household, or settlement involved.
societies.leadershipStructure: No single ruler is established for the whole region. Leadership is local.
societies.decisionMaking: Local custom, household decisions, councils, elders, leaders, or consensus depending on the community.
societies.customs: No single regional custom is imposed. Local customs should be authored within individual societies.
societies.beliefs: Varied and intentionally open until established by canon.
societies.languageDialect: Multiple local dialects and ways of speaking may exist.
societies.livelihood: Hunting, gathering, farming, fishing, craft, trade, animal keeping, and other pre-industrial work according to place.

societies.name: Whispering Woods Clans
societies.description: A starter grouping for families and clans living in or regularly using Whispering Woods. It exists so the region has inhabitants without inventing a single finished culture for them.
societies.origin: Long-term settlement and seasonal use of the forest and its waterways.
societies.territoryNotes: Forest use and territory can overlap between families and clans and should be refined as canon is added.
societies.seasonalMovement: Some households may move between forest resources seasonally; this is not universal.
societies.kinshipBasis: Family, clan, adoption, guardianship, and local bonds.
societies.membershipRules: Defined by each constituent family or clan.
societies.leadershipStructure: Local family or clan leadership rather than a single forest ruler.
societies.decisionMaking: Local custom and agreement between affected families or clans.
societies.customs: Forest-specific customs remain open for authored canon.
societies.beliefs: Not yet fixed as a single shared belief system.
societies.languageDialect: Local forest dialects may differ between groups.
societies.livelihood: Hunting, gathering, fishing, small farming, craft, and trade suited to the forest.

societies.name: Bitterroot Orphanage Household
societies.description: The caretakers and residents associated with Bitterroot Orphanage, represented as a household rather than a blood family.
societies.origin: Formed around the orphanage and the need to house and care for young residents without stable family homes.
societies.kinshipBasis: Guardianship, foster ties, found family, friendship, and shared residence.
societies.membershipRules: Residents, caretakers, and others formally belonging to the orphanage household.
societies.leadershipStructure: Caretaking authority within the institution; exact roles and individuals remain open for canon.
societies.customs: Household routines and traditions remain open for authored canon.
societies.beliefs: No single belief system is assumed.
societies.languageDialect: Reflects the varied backgrounds of residents and caretakers.
societies.livelihood: Maintaining the orphanage through local work, supplies, craft, food production, and community support.

societies.name: Bitterroot Bluffs Bands
societies.description: A starter grouping for small communities and travelling bands associated with Bitterroot Bluffs.
societies.origin: Local habitation and travel through the bluff country.
societies.territoryNotes: Specific borders and named groups are intentionally left open.
societies.seasonalMovement: May vary with weather, food, and local routes.
societies.kinshipBasis: Family, affinity, adoption, and band membership.
societies.livelihood: Hunting, craft, trade, gathering, herding, and other work suited to the bluffs.

societies.name: Bitterroot Peak Clans
societies.description: A starter grouping for inhabitants associated with Bitterroot Peak and its high country.
societies.origin: Long-term adaptation to the mountain region and its routes.
societies.territoryNotes: Specific clan borders and settlements remain open for canon.
societies.seasonalMovement: Movement may follow weather and access through the high country.
societies.kinshipBasis: Family, clan, adoption, and local bonds.
societies.livelihood: Hunting, gathering, craft, trade, animal keeping, and other high-country work.

societies.name: Brackenjaw Enclave
societies.description: The Brackenjaw community of Splitpine Reach. Brackenjaw is a community identity, not a species; Ragna and Pip Holt are werewolves who belong to this enclave.
societies.origin: An established local community in Splitpine Reach.
societies.territoryNotes: The enclave maintains and watches marked boundaries in Splitpine Reach.
societies.seasonalMovement: Settled community with patrol activity across surrounding trails and boundaries.
societies.kinshipBasis: Families, households, community ties, duty, and local belonging.
societies.membershipRules: Membership is based on belonging to the Brackenjaw community rather than species alone.
societies.leadershipStructure: Local enclave authority supported by specialist roles such as Boundary Wardens.
societies.decisionMaking: Local community authority and practical duty structures.
societies.customs: Boundary markers, patrol routines, local chores, preparedness, and practical responsibility are established parts of daily life around the ranger station.
societies.beliefs: Not yet fixed as a single shared belief system.
societies.languageDialect: Local Brackenjaw speech and ranger terminology.
societies.livelihood: Pre-industrial settlement work, ranger duties, craft, food production, hunting, trade, and maintenance of local trails and boundaries.

families.name: Holt
families.description: The Holt family of Brackenjaw Enclave. Ragna Holt is Pip Holt's mother. They are their own Bitterroot family and are not Whiteclaws.

people.name: Ragna Holt
people.description: 41-year-old upright feral werewolf, veteran Boundary Warden, and mother of Pip Holt. Ragna is hard, terse, territorial, proactive, observant, highly competent, and protective through action rather than speeches. She judges outsiders by what they do after being warned, checks facts instead of dismissing credible danger, and remains the adult authority when Pip is involved.

people.name: Pip Holt
people.description: 12-year-old upright feral werewolf and Ragna Holt's daughter. Pip is a scrappy, brave, stubborn, observant, eager, tomboyish would-be Boundary Warden. She copies Ragna's stance and ranger phrases, knows familiar trails, markers, chores and gear surprisingly well, but remains twelve in judgment, authority, knowledge and emotional regulation. Her confidence often outruns what she can safely handle.

relationships.notes: Mother and daughter with very high trust and affection. Pip admires Ragna intensely and copies her ranger mannerisms while pushing against restrictions. Ragna loves Pip fiercely but shows care through rules, chores, limits, instruction, protection, and intervention rather than becoming generically soft.

memories.title: When the Howling Hills Drowned
memories.description: A catastrophic flood changed the Howling Hills, drowning valleys, altering routes, and leaving scars that continue to shape travel, settlement, and memory.
persistentEffects: Some old routes and low ground remain drowned or difficult to cross.
Communities remember the flood as a major turning point in the region.
The landscape still carries visible flood scars and changed waterways.

seasons.name: Spring
seasons.weatherPrompt: Rapid thaws, heavy rain, swollen rivers, mud, sudden cold snaps, and dangerous storm fronts are common.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.weatherPrompt: Warm periods can break violently into thunderstorms, high winds, torrential rain, flash flooding, and abrupt temperature drops.

seasons.name: Autumn
seasons.weatherPrompt: Storm frequency rises as temperatures fall. Strong winds, prolonged rain, early snow at elevation, and difficult travel are common.

seasons.name: Winter
seasons.weatherPrompt: Severe cold, heavy snow, blizzards, ice, whiteout conditions, and dangerous wind chill are credible seasonal hazards.

timeWeather.climate: Temperate wilderness with violent and unstable weather, strong regional variation, and harsher conditions at elevation.
timeWeather.weatherPrompt: Bitterroot weather is natural rather than magical by default, but it is notably violent, unstable, and dangerous. Storms can intensify quickly. Heavy rain, flooding, landslides, strong winds, lightning, sudden cold snaps, heavy snow, and blizzards should occur when season and region make them plausible. Weather should meaningfully affect visibility, travel, shelter, work, wildlife, and character decisions.
